\texttt{brax\_\allowbreak 2021} & rigid bodies in maximal coordinates; naive/quadratic-scaling pairwise collision detection (no broad-phase acceleration structure); no convex-decomposition or mesh-vs-primitive distinction described & not LCP-based; velocity-level collision updates with Baumgarte stabilization (inspired by the Tiny Differentiable Simulator); joints modeled as spring constraints rather than Featherstone-style articulated-body methods \\
\texttt{comfree\_\allowbreak sim\_\allowbreak 2026} & complementarity-free, analytical (closed-form) contact resolution in the dual cone of the Coulomb friction cone via a prediction-correction/impedance-style update, extended to a unified 6D model (normal, tangential, torsional, rolling friction) & no complementarity solve; a 4-kernel GPU pipeline (Algorithm 1: smooth-velocity prediction, per-contact/per-face dual-cone solve, generalized-impulse accumulation, velocity correction) computes the impulse in closed form per contact facet \\
\texttt{dojo\_\allowbreak 2022} & hard-contact nonlinear complementarity problem (NCP) with an exact nonlinear (second-order-cone) friction cone, avoiding pyramidal/linearized approximation, to avoid interpenetration and creep artifacts & custom primal-dual interior-point solver (Algorithm 2), based on Mehrotra's predictor-corrector algorithm, extended for non-Euclidean quaternion variables, with cone-handling borrowed from CVXOPT; gradients via implicit differentiation (implicit function theorem) of the KKT/complementarity system, with central-path parameter kappa trading gradient smoothness for physical accuracy \\
\texttt{genesis\_\allowbreak 2024} & Constraint-based rigid solver (equality/inequality constraints, plus an explicit noslip() post-pass, architecturally similar to MuJoCo's solver+noslip design) combined with multi-material coupling: FEM, MPM, particle-based PBD and SPH, a libuipc Incremental Potential Contact solver, an explicit inter-solver coupler, and a SAP (semi-analytic-primal-style) compliant-contact path used for grasp-coupling scenes. & ConstraintSolver with Newton-style line-search iterative resolve (linesearch.py) and constraint-island decomposition for parallelism (island.py); multiple pluggable physics solvers (Rigid, FEM, MPM, PBD, SPH, libuipc, SAP) compiled via the Quadrants (Taichi-derived) backend. \\
\texttt{isaacgym\_\allowbreak 2021} & Rigid-body contacts via PhysX; contact geometry can be primitive shapes or meshes loaded from URDF/MJCF (Sec. 2.2); net contact forces exposed per-rigid-body via the Tensor API (Table 1, Get-only). No explicit statement of convex-vs-mesh contact generation or per-pair contact-point count. Shadow Hand tendons simulated via PhysX Fixed Tendon mechanics: spring+damping force proportional to deviation from rest length, propagated through a tendon-joint tree (Sec. 3, Appendix A.1). & Temporal Gauss-Seidel (TGS) solver (Sec. 3, ref. 18), not classic PGS/LCP: folds sub-stepping into a per-body accumulated velocity-delta buffer projected onto the constraint Jacobians. Table 3 exposes two user-tunable iteration knobs, Position iterations (biased, velocity+positional-error-correcting) and Velocity iterations (unbiased, velocity-error-only-correcting); no default numeric values for these are given in the main text. \\
\texttt{isaaclab\_\allowbreak 2025} & Rigid contacts by default via PhysX 5 (SDF collisions, Featherstone articulation solver, Sec. 2.2); `Factory` assembly envs specifically use 'SDF-based contact generation, a contact reduction technique, and a Gauss-Seidel solver' (Sec. 6.4). ContactSensor exposes net normal force per body, optional filtered pairs, contact duration, average contact point, and a short history (Sec. 3.3.1); no contact-quality/penetration metric is defined (survey note). & NVIDIA PhysX 5's internal rigid-body/Featherstone-articulation solver, used as-is; Factory assembly envs specifically named as using a Gauss-Seidel solver with SDF-based contact generation and contact reduction (Sec. 6.4). No timestep, decimation, or solver-iteration values are stated anywhere in the paper for the general (dexterous) suite; the only note is qualitative, that the Digit humanoid 'requires a higher solver iteration count for stable simulation' (Fig. 14). \\
\texttt{maniskill3\_\allowbreak 2024} & PhysX (via SAPIEN) rigid-body contacts on GPU; no statement of convex-vs-mesh contact generation or contact-point count in the note. AllegroHandRightTouch reads FSR contact impulse (`get\_fsr\_impulse`) for touch sensing (App. VII-H, code). & PhysX (via SAPIEN), used as-is; no LCP/PGS/TGS/Newton solver-algorithm name given. Benchmark (cartpole) settings state 'Solver Position Iterations: 4 / Solver Velocity Iterations: 0' (App. XI-A), but per-task `\_default\_sim\_config` values are not exported in the parsed source. \\
\texttt{mujoco\_\allowbreak 2012} & soft, convex velocity-stepping contact; three interchangeable solvers replace the standard LCP-with-friction-pyramid approach: implicit-complementarity, convex (kinetic-energy minimization with a soft non-penetration cost), and diagonal (mass-aware spring-damper) & implicit-complementarity solver (customized non-smooth Newton method, most accurate); convex solver (interior-point method used for reported timings; projected Newton/CG/Gauss-Seidel also mentioned as unverified-faster alternatives); diagonal solver (per-contact critically-damped spring-damper using the diagonal of the A matrix, fastest/least accurate) \\
\texttt{mujoco\_\allowbreak convex\_\allowbreak contact\_\allowbreak 2014} & soft, convex, complementarity-free; a unified impulse vector covers joint dry friction, joint/tendon/distance limits, and frictional contacts together, with an elliptical friction cone whose dimensionality per contact is 2 (sliding), 3, or 5 (sliding+torsional+rolling) & GPGS (generalized projected Gauss-Seidel, described as the authors' own unpublished-at-the-time method handling cone and pyramid constraints) for the contact/limit impulse; a separate 'soft Gauss principle' derivation for equality/holonomic constraints; an analytically-invertible closed-form solver for a restricted circular-cone special case \\
\texttt{mujoco\_\allowbreak warp\_\allowbreak 2025} & MuJoCo's native solref/solimp-parameterized soft-constraint contact model ported to Warp --- per-contact Jacobian construction (dense and sparse variants, with flex variants) and equality/limit/friction constraint rows; not a re-derived contact model & MuJoCo's default (implicit CCP-style) solver and Newton constraint solver (via a 'newton' flag threaded through equality/limit/friction kernels) are supported; legacy PGS solver and noslip post-processing pass are 'not yet supported' per the README \\
\texttt{newton\_\allowbreak 2025} & Solver-dependent: MuJoCo-style soft-constraint (solref/solimp-style) contact via SolverMuJoCo/MJWarp; Proximal-ADMM / Dual-Variational-Inequality contact resolution via SolverKamino; position-based-dynamics-style constraint projection for the XPBD and VBD solvers. & Multi-solver architecture: SolverMuJoCo (wraps MJWarp), SolverKamino (Proximal-ADMM + DVI), XPBD (rigid), VBD (cloth/deformables), Style3D (cloth), plus a separate IKSolver (LM and L-BFGS backends). \\
\texttt{orbit\_\allowbreak 2023} & PhysX SDK 5 signed-distance-field (SDF) collision checking for rigid bodies (handles non-convex geometry such as screw threads); FEM-based solver using a constraint-based stable neo-hookean material formulation for deformable bodies; PBD (position-based dynamics) solver for cloth & PhysX SDK 5's internal rigid-body and FEM solvers, used as-is; no LCP/PGS/TGS, Newton, or CG iteration counts given \\
\texttt{pybullet\_\allowbreak 2016} & \na & \na \\
\texttt{raisim\_\allowbreak 2018} & \na & \na \\
\texttt{sapien\_\allowbreak 2020} & Rigid-body contact with convex-decomposed collision meshes (PhysX 4.1); three joint systems offered (kinematic, dynamic, and PhysX articulation) trading control accuracy against speed. & PhysX 4.1's internal rigid-body solver, used as-is; no LCP/PGS/TGS name or iteration count given in the paper. \\
